newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Study reveals why women spend longer in toilet.
newsitem.headline: Study reveals why women spend longer in toilet.

text.p: Ever wondered by women spend more time in the toilet than men? An Australian study has found perennial queues outside women's public toilets are exacerbated by women's embarassment and hygiene concerns.

Women spend time lining toilet bowls with paper to muffle any noise and "hovered" over toilet bowls because they do not want to touch the seat, said Sarah Wallis, an industrial design student at the University of New South Wales.

Many women also did not like touching flush buttons or door handles with their bare hands and had trouble finding somewhere to put personal belongings like bags and wallets, Wallis found in a six-month study sponsored by toilet maker Coroma.

"Some may wipe the seat, some cover it with paper, some put paper into the bowl or flush the toilet to cover any noises that might be made," Wallis told Reuters, adding this all meant longer time spent, longer queues and wasted paper and water.

To address their needs, Wallis designed La Prima -- a slim-line china toilet which women can stand over to use, which comes with an in-built sanitary disposal unit, a flush foot pedal, and a stainless steel shelf to hold personal belongings.
Wallis said further research was needed to see whether her project, currently on display at a Sydney exhibition, had commercial application.
